description: Issue #839: a Heritage short alias is a built-in name at run time, exactly as illegal to declare as the canonical it spells. The runtime resolves the alias to its canonical and re-runs the same lookup rather than consulting a table of its own (`spec/conformance.md:150`, Heritage is "alternate spellings only"), so `define fd` is `ol-reserved-word` because `define forward` is. The empty event stream is what makes this discriminating: `999` would mean the learner's procedure ran, and a `move` event would mean the turtle did. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.

diagnostics.message: fd is already part of OpenLogo. choose another name.
